content: 1. Tapentadol has been shown to provide long-term pain relief in patients suffering from chronic low back pain, with an associated reduction in segmental sensitization. 2. The combination of oxycodone and naloxone in prolonged-release tablets has demonstrated both analgesic efficacy and safety in patients experiencing moderate to severe chronic pain. 3. Extended-release tramadol (tramadol ER) has been effective in managing chronic low back pain. 4. Oxytrex, a combination therapy, minimizes physical dependence while delivering effective analgesia, as evidenced by a randomized controlled trial in patients with low back pain. 5. Treatment with ALO-02, an extended-release formulation of oxycodone and sequestered naltrexone, has been associated with improvements in patient-reported health-related quality of life, work productivity, and activity impairment in individuals with moderate-to-severe chronic low back pain. 6. The WHO guidelines recommend non-surgical management strategies for chronic primary low back pain in adults, particularly in primary and community care settings. 7. A multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial has confirmed the efficacy and safety of single-entity, once-daily hydrocodone tablets in patients with uncontrolled moderate-to-severe chronic low back pain. 8. A 7-day buprenorphine transdermal system has been shown to improve health-related quality of life in opioid-naïve patients with moderate-to-severe chronic low back pain, as demonstrated in a randomized, placebo-controlled study. 9. Subgroup analysis revealed that patients with chronic low back pain and comorbid depression did not exhibit a diminished response to buprenorphine transdermal system treatment. 10. The buprenorphine transdermal system has been found to reduce functional interference in patients with chronic low back pain compared to placebo. 11. A study comparing morphine, nortriptyline, and their combination versus placebo in patients with chronic lumbar root pain demonstrated significant analgesic effects. 12. Tramadol treatment has been shown to enhance aerobic exercise capacity in individuals with chronic non-specific low back pain. 13. Etoricoxib, a selective COX-2 inhibitor, has been effective in reducing pain and disability in patients with chronic low back pain, as evidenced by a randomized, placebo-controlled, 3-month trial. 14. Tanezumab has demonstrated efficacy and safety in the treatment of chronic low back pain, as shown in multiple randomized controlled trials. 15. Naproxen sodium and diflunisal have been evaluated against placebo for their effectiveness in managing chronic back pain, with positive outcomes reported. 16. Indomethacin and flurbiprofen have been compared to placebo in a double-blind crossover trial for lumbar spondylosis management, showing significant benefits. 17. A clinical trial with PF-06372865, a selective GABAA positive allosteric modulator, demonstrated its potential in managing chronic low back pain. 18. Duloxetine monotherapy has been shown to be effective in Japanese patients with chronic low back pain, as evidenced by a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial. 19. Duloxetine has consistently demonstrated efficacy and safety in managing chronic low back pain across multiple randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials. 20. Noradrenergic and serotonergic antidepressants have shown efficacy in reducing chronic low back pain intensity in concentration-controlled trials. 21. Desipramine, cognitive behavioral therapy, and active placebo therapy have been evaluated in a randomized, placebo-controlled trial for low back pain, with significant findings. 22. Low-dose amitriptyline has been shown to be effective in managing chronic low back pain in a randomized clinical trial. 23. Paroxetine has been studied for its effects on the relationship between pain and depression in chronic low back pain patients, with promising results. 24. Gabapentin has been found to reduce chronic benign nociceptive pain in a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study. 25. Topiramate has been evaluated for its efficacy in treating chronic low back pain in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, showing positive outcomes. 26. Botulinum toxin type A has been investigated for its efficacy in treating chronic low back pain, with multiple studies supporting its use. 27. Acupuncture combined with baclofen has been shown to reduce chronic non-specific low back pain in a randomized controlled clinical trial. 28. Dexamethasone phosphate has been evaluated for its usefulness in the conservative treatment of lumbar pain in a double-blind study, with favorable results. 29. Local injection therapies, including bupivacaine and lidocaine, have been studied for their effectiveness in managing chronic low back pain, with significant findings. 30. Herbal medicines, such as Harpagophytum procumbens and willow bark extract, have demonstrated efficacy in treating acute and chronic low back pain in randomized, double-blind studies. 31. Capsaicin cream and plasters have been shown to be effective and safe for managing chronic low back pain in multiple clinical trials. 32. Ginger and vitamin D3 supplementation have been compared for their effects on inflammatory markers and pain severity in adults with low back pain, with positive outcomes reported. 33. Traditional Thai massage and herbal compress massage have been evaluated for their effectiveness in elderly patients with low back pain, showing significant benefits. 34. A Persian remedy involving white lily in sesame oil has shown promising pain-relieving activity in patients with chronic low back pain. 35. Weight management strategies, including water-based aerobic training and intermittent dieting, have been shown to improve pain and functional outcomes in obese patients with chronic low back pain.
